---
id: SA-0358
title: Nothing pins the spec-writer send-back prompt's wording, so a drifting edit reaches the writer unseen
type: bug
priority: 3
estimated_lines: 16
estimate_measured: true
touches:
  - tests/test_context.py
forbidden:
  - DESIGN.md
  - CONTEXT.md
  - CLAUDE.md
  - README.md
  - pyproject.toml
  - uv.lock
  - .saffron/**
  - .claude/**
  - ontology/**
  - tests/ontology/**
  - docs/**

  - harness/**

  - saffron/agents/prompts/turns/spec-writer-send-back.md
  - saffron/spec_review.py
  - saffron/agents/context.py
  - saffron/cli.py
  - tests/test_spec_review.py
  - tests/test_cli.py
budget_usd: 15
max_attempts: 3
max_turns: 40
risk: standard
acceptance:
  - claim: >-
      `spec_review.SPEC_WRITER_SEND_BACK_PROMPT` loads
      `saffron/agents/prompts/turns/spec-writer-send-back.md` through
      `context.turn_prompt("spec-writer-send-back")`
      (`saffron/spec_review.py:533`, `saffron/agents/context.py:283-298`).
      `SA-0353`'s own notes ask that file for one or two sentences telling
      the writer the host found the faults below and to fix every one of
      them in the spec, keeping everything else about it the same, and to
      stay free of any repo path or tool name
      (`.saffron/specs/SA-0353-a-writers-draft-reaches-the-finish-unparsed-because-no-gate-reads-it-inside-its-own-session.md:333-336`).
      None of the three tests that read `TURN_PROMPTS` pins that wording:
      the census checks only that the file is a member
      (`tests/test_context.py:707-709`), the round trip compares the
      constant to its own loader so any text agrees with itself
      (`tests/test_context.py:712-718`), and the slot check looks only for
      an unfilled `{...}` (`tests/test_context.py:721-727`). The witness
      reads the constant directly, asserts it equals its two sentences
      exactly, that it holds no `/`, and that it names none of `pytest`,
      `git`, `python` or `saffron`.
    witness: tests/test_context.py::test_the_send_back_prompt_asks_the_writer_to_fix_every_fault_and_names_no_path_or_tool
    wrong_versions:
      - "The file names a repo path, such as `.saffron/specs/`, inside its second sentence."
      - "The file names a tool, such as `pytest` or `git`, rather than staying free of one."
      - The file keeps only its first sentence and drops the request to fix every fault.
      - The file asks the writer to fix only the first fault rather than every one.
      - The file tells the writer to fix every fault in the code rather than in the spec.
      - The file drops its closing clause and never asks the writer to keep everything else about it the same.
---

## Context

Review of `SA-0354`'s merge, `13ddf0298406e705fc61f49c9c2c12ce00a575e8`. That
spec's own `touches` names only `saffron/cli.py` and `tests/test_cli.py`
(`SA-0354`'s frontmatter). Its true diff, `git diff
b360ff34..13ddf0298406e705fc61f49c9c2c12ce00a575e8`, touches exactly those
two files and nothing else. A wider diff taken from an earlier point in the
stack shows `saffron/agents/prompts/turns/spec-writer-send-back.md` as
newly added too, but that file belongs to `SA-0353`. `SA-0353` merged at
`abcc49f6` before `SA-0354` started. `SA-0353`'s own `touches` names that
file
(`.saffron/specs/SA-0353-a-writers-draft-reaches-the-finish-unparsed-because-no-gate-reads-it-inside-its-own-session.md:9-16`).
`SA-0354` neither claims it nor mentions it in its acceptance criteria or
notes. This spec leaves that file itself untouched. It closes a gap in
what tests it, found while tracing that file's ownership.

**The prompt and its loader.** `saffron/spec_review.py:533` sets
`SPEC_WRITER_SEND_BACK_PROMPT = context.turn_prompt("spec-writer-send-back")`.
`context.turn_prompt` reads `prompts/turns/<name>.md`, strips trailing
newlines, and fills any `{extraction}` slot
(`saffron/agents/context.py:283-298`). The file holds no such slot. So the
constant is exactly the file's two sentences with the trailing newline
stripped. Reading the file's raw bytes at the base confirms this: `The
host found the faults below in the spec you wrote. Fix every one of\nthem
in the spec and keep everything else about it the same.`

**What `SA-0353` asked for and never pinned.** `SA-0353`'s own notes
describe the file's required content: "The file holds one or two
sentences. They say the host found the faults below, and ask the writer
to fix every one in the spec. Keep it free of any repo path or tool
name."
(`.saffron/specs/SA-0353-a-writers-draft-reaches-the-finish-unparsed-because-no-gate-reads-it-inside-its-own-session.md:333-336`).
`SA-0353`'s own acceptance criteria exercise `SPEC_WRITER_SEND_BACK_PROMPT`
only as an opaque string concatenated onto fault lines
(`tests/test_spec_review.py`'s `_run_writer`-based witnesses, e.g.
`test_a_draft_with_faults_goes_back_to_the_same_session_naming_each_line`).
None of them assert its own wording.

**What `tests/test_context.py` checks today.** `TURN_PROMPTS` carries the
constant under the key `"spec-writer-send-back"`
(`tests/test_context.py:703`). Three parametrized tests read that dict.
`test_every_turn_prompt_file_is_loaded_by_something` checks only that the
directory's filenames equal the dict's keys
(`tests/test_context.py:707-709`). `test_a_turn_prompt_constant_is_its_file`
asserts `constant == context.turn_prompt(name)`. That holds for any file
content at all, since both sides come from the same loader
(`tests/test_context.py:712-718`).
`test_a_loaded_turn_prompt_keeps_no_unfilled_slot` only looks for a
bracketed `{...}` (`tests/test_context.py:721-727`). None of the three
would notice the file naming a path or a tool, dropping a sentence, or
narrowing "every one" to "the first". Measured at the base, a copy of the
file still passes every one of those three tests. That copy has a repo
path inserted, a tool named, and its second sentence dropped. The same
holds for a copy with its "every one" narrowed to "the first". It also
holds for a copy with "in the spec" changed to "in the code", or with its
closing clause dropped. Each such copy still passes
`tests/test_context.py` in full (78 tests, unmodified), and `ruff
check`/`ruff format --check` on the file.

**Other work on this file.** `SA-0356` is still open
(`.saffron/specs/SA-0356-a-batch-stops-at-the-first-candidate-its-budget-cannot-cover-though-a-later-one-fits.md`)
and does not touch `tests/test_context.py`. No other spec under
`.saffron/specs/` names it either.

## Problem

Add one witness to `tests/test_context.py` that reads
`spec_review.SPEC_WRITER_SEND_BACK_PROMPT` directly. It checks two things.
First, that the constant equals its exact two sentences. Second, that it
names no `/` and none of `pytest`, `git`, `python` or `saffron`. Place it
beside the other `TURN_PROMPTS`-reading tests, after
`test_a_loaded_turn_prompt_keeps_no_unfilled_slot`.

## Out of scope

- **Editing the prompt file.** Its current content already satisfies the
  witness. Nothing here changes it. It is `forbidden`.
- **A repo-wide rule.** Only this one prompt gets a wording witness here.
  Generalizing "no repo path or tool name" to every entry in
  `TURN_PROMPTS` is a separate spec's work, not implied by this one.
- **`saffron/spec_review.py` or `saffron/agents/context.py`.** Both load
  the constant correctly today. Neither is touched.

## Notes for the agent

**Existing code, not new.** The prompt file and the constant it loads
already exist, unchanged by this spec. So the criterion names
`wrong_versions` against the file's own wording. Each one is a plausible
wrong edit a later change to the file could make. `witness` reports a
real pass or fail for each, rather than a `skip`.

**`spec_review` needs no new import.** `tests/test_context.py` already
imports it at module scope (`tests/test_context.py:8`), used by the
existing `TURN_PROMPTS` dict two names above this one.

**The witness.** A plain `def`, with no parametrization. This test is
about one specific file's wording, not a loop over every prompt's.
Compare `spec_review.SPEC_WRITER_SEND_BACK_PROMPT` to the literal two-line
string. Use a single Python string with one embedded `\n`, not two
concatenated literals split across the dropped trailing newline. Then
assert `"/" not in text`, and that none of `"pytest"`, `"git"`,
`"python"`, `"saffron"` appears in `text.lower()`.

**Measured on a prototype**, at the base
`13ddf0298406e705fc61f49c9c2c12ce00a575e8`. The one-test addition passed
with the source as it stands. `tests/test_context.py` passed in full (78
tests). `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` passed on the changed
file. Each of the six `wrong_versions` was applied by hand to a copy of
the prompt file. Each one failed the new witness. The other 77 tests in
`tests/test_context.py` stayed green, confirming they are not caught
today. The diff measured 110 changed tokens by `size_gate`, against the
`bug` ceiling of 1300. `estimated_lines` is the diff's own 16 inserted
lines.
